evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/documents/shares.rs:574 access_protected_share -- public, unauthenticated endpoint (mounted via shares::public_router at POST /api/v1/documents/shared/{token}/access, lib.rs:165 merge) verifies a caller-supplied share password (verify_share_password_for_share at ~L617) with NO brute-force protection: no failed-attempt counter, no per-token/per-IP lockout, no throttle. grep for rate.?limit|throttle|attempt|lockout across routes/documents/ returns 0 hits.

The only rate limiter in api-server is a per-TENANT set (state.tenant_rate_limiters: TenantRateLimiterSet, applied through host_tenant_middleware keyed on org context). The share handler comment explicitly states 'This public endpoint has no caller org context', so the per-tenant limiter cannot key these unauthenticated requests -> the password endpoint is effectively unthrottled. An attacker holding a share token can brute-force the share password at request speed.

The parallel signer endpoint (routes/signatures::public_sign_router) and other public flows should be checked for the same gap. Fix: add per-token (and/or per-IP) attempt throttling + exponential backoff/lockout on access_protected_share before verify, or gate the public_router behind a dedicated unauthenticated-rate-limit layer.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/documents/shares.rs:437 & :574 -- both public share handlers derive the audit ip_address from axum ConnectInfo<SocketAddr> (let ip_address = addr.ip().to_string()) and persist it via log_share_access_for_share(LogShareAccess{ ip_address, .. }).

ConnectInfo is the DIRECT TCP peer. In this deployment the api-server sits behind a reverse proxy / load balancer (per repo architecture: nginx + *.dev.ppt.rlt.sk), so addr.ip() is the proxy's address for every request -- the share-access audit log records the proxy IP, not the real client, for all public document-share accesses.

The code comments call this write 'important for audit trail', but the recorded IP is not attacker-attributable and is identical across all clients, undermining the audit value and defeating any future IP-based abuse detection. Fix: resolve the client IP from a validated forwarded-for chain (trusted-proxy-aware, e.g. axum-client-ip / a checked X-Forwarded-For) instead of the raw socket peer.
